'''Ator''' was a [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]] located just inside the [[Horizon]] boundary of the [[Deep Core/Legends|Deep Core]] that featured [[City/Legends|urban]] terrain. Around [[4200 BBY]], pilgrims from Ator [[Colonist/Legends|colonized]] the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]] world [[Arkanis/Legends|Arkanis]], which eventually became the [[Capital/Legends|capital]] of the small [[Regency Worlds/Legends|Arkanis Regency]] empire. [[Millennium/Legends|Millennia]] later, the [[Moisture farmer/Legends|moisture farmer]] [[Cliegg Lars/Legends|Cliegg Lars]] left [[Lars family/Legends|his family's]] [[Lars homestead/Legends|homestead]] on the planet [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]] and settled on Ator. There, Cliegg [[Marriage/Legends|married]] [[Aika Lars/Legends|Aika]] and had a [[Gender/Legends|son]], [[Owen Lars/Legends|Owen]], but after Aika's unexpected [[Death/Legends|death]], Cliegg returned to Tatooine with Owen.

==Description==
Ator was a terrestrial [[Planet/Legends|planet]]<ref name="FF72" /> located in the [[Ator system/Legends|Ator system]]. It lay in the [[Arrowhead]] region, a part of [[The Slice/Legends|the Slice]] portion of the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]]. Ator was situated just inside the [[Horizon]]&mdash;a mathematically set boundary at which making [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] jumps using outdated [[Astrocartography|astrocartographic]] data fell below the safe margin of error of [[Starship/Legends|starship]] [[Navigation computer/Legends|navicomputers]] due to [[Realspace/Legends|space]] travel dangers inherent to the [[Deep Core/Legends|Deep Core]]&mdash;but was still classified as part of the Core Worlds instead of the Deep Core due to the Ator [[Star system/Legends|system]] being an established part of the Core culturally and historically.<ref name="TEA" /> Ator featured [[City/Legends|urban]] terrain<ref name="FF72" /> of which bright lights were a part.<ref name="DB Cliegg">{{DB|character|cliegglars|Lars, Cliegg}}</ref>

==History==
[[Atorese]] pilgrims [[Colonist/Legends|settled]] the world [[Arkanis/Legends|Arkanis]], a part of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories']] [[Arkanis sector/Legends|Arkanis sector]], around [[4200 BBY]], with the [[Sector/Legends|sector's]] planets [[Vasch]] and [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]] being first colonized around the same [[Time/Legends|time]]. Eventually, contact between Arkanis and the Core was lost, and other colonies established by people from Ator withered and died. Arkanis survived, however, as the [[Capital/Legends|capital]] of a small empire known as the [[Regency Worlds/Legends|Arkanis Regency]], with Atorese colonists also founding the Regency Worlds [[Agriworld/Legends|agriworld]] [[New Ator]] around [[80 BBY/Legends|80 BBY]].<ref name="TEA" />

[[File:Owen-OP.jpg|thumb|left|300px|The future Tatooine moisture farmer Owen Lars was born on Ator.]]
When [[Cliegg Lars/Legends|Cliegg Lars]], the [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|son]] of a [[Lars family/Legends|family]] of Tatooine [[Moisture farmer/Legends|moisture farmers]]<ref name="FF72" /> who was [[Reproduction/Legends|born]] in [[82 BBY/Legends|82 BBY]],<ref name="FF140">{{FactFile|140|FAM 1-2|Skywalker Family Tree}}</ref> became old enough, he, having grown disenchanted with the hard life of [[Moisture farm/Legends|moisture farming]] and enticed by the allure of Core Worlds cities, left Tatooine for Ator. There, he met and [[Marriage/Legends|married]] [[Aika Lars/Legends|Aika]], with whom he had a Human son, [[Owen Lars/Legends|Owen]],<ref name="FF72" /> who was born in [[52 BBY/Legends|52 BBY]]. Cliegg and Aika struggled to raise their [[Youngling/Legends|child]] in the confines of their living quarters, and Cliegg eventually realized that the stability of life at his family's [[Lars homestead/Legends|homestead]] on Tatooine would prove to be a significantly more beneficial environment for both Aika and Owen.<ref name="FF140" />

Cliegg began to consider leaving Ator with his family for Tatooine, but tragedy struck when Aika [[Death/Legends|died]] unexpectedly. With nothing to keep him in the Core Worlds anymore, Cliegg took Owen and returned to his family's [[Farm/Legends|farm]] on Tatooine,<ref name="FF140" /> also taking a [[Thornen Pyramid Puzzle/Legends|Thornen Pyramid Puzzle]] with him.<ref name="CL">[[Star Wars: Complete Locations (2005)|''Star Wars: Complete Locations'']]</ref> Eventually, Owen himself became a moisture [[Farmer/Legends|farmer]].<ref name="FF140" /> He remembered little of Ator,<ref name="DB Cliegg" /> but as late as the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], the Thornen Pyramid Puzzle from the planet was nevertheless kept in his and his wife [[Beru Whitesun Lars/Legends|Beru's]] [[Sleeper (furniture)|bedroom]] at the Lars homestead.<ref name="CL" />

==Locations==
Ator was the site of a [[Standard century/Legends|centuries]]-old [[Skyscraper/Legends|skyscraper]]. It had a cramped<ref name="TCVD" /> and [[Claustrophobia/Legends|claustrophobic]]<ref name="FF72" /> attic apartment where Cliegg Lars and his family lived.<ref name="TCVD" />

==Behind the scenes==
Ator was first mentioned in the [[2002]] reference book ''[[Star Wars: Attack of the Clones: The Visual Dictionary]]'' by [[David West Reynolds (real person)|David West Reynolds]].<ref name="AotCVD">''[[Star Wars: Attack of the Clones: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> The [[2009]] reference book ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' placed Ator in grid square M-10.<ref name="TEA" />
